Here's one for ya: Paperback books.

Now, I like books as much as the next man, but I hate paperbacks. If I have the money, I will buy the more expensive hardback version (if a hardback version exists), but I usually don't have the money.

Anyway, onto the rant:

Problem number one:
After reading a paperback, the covers will invariably splay out so that it looks like a V from the bottom. This simply doesn't look good sitting on a table, and makes them much more difficult to put back onto a shelf.

Problem number two:
I like to hold a book flat, so that the pages are at a 180 degree angle to each other. This works excellently for hardbacks, but will ruin the spine of a paperback. By the time I'm finished with it, there are tons of ugly white creases running down the spine. It's terrible.

Problem number three:
If I put a hardback book into a backpack or some other sort of bag, the covers will come out looking exactly the same as when they went in. If I put a paperback into a bag, the covers will get folded back, and creased backwards, completely ruining the cover. Sure, you can put it on a shelf, hoping that the pressure will put the cover back to its original glory, but it will still leave that bumpy white line, forever serving as a reminder of that one time you were slightly more clumsy than usual while packing.

Problem number four:
You know what? The sounds of paperbacks aren't right. When I put a hardback book onto my nightstand when I'm done reading, it makes a nice clunk, and when I slam it closed after finishing it, it makes a nice sturdy wumf. When I put a paperback onto my nightstand, it goes blum. What the hell is blum? I didn't pay for blum, I paid for clunk. And when I slam it closed, it goes splap. That's a terrible book closing sound. It's an amazing bitch-slapping sound, but I don't want to slap the shit out of my books. I'll gladly wumf them, but I don't want to splap them.

Anyway, that's what I chose to rant about for some reason.
